summary: B7 after-hours Webull ladder exits (re-review of b617c9c9 after my change request on 3828924f). Range-diff vs the reviewed head: commits 1-3 byte-identical after rebase onto 52f4e940; one new commit limited to the three requested items + body (unexercised_watch.py allowlist + page body, service.py new source webull_eh_ladder_unsold + 20:00 branch + _page_webull_eh_ladder_unsold, tests). Production logic (carried from my first review): outside RTH, CW_FLOOR / CW_HARD_STOP / V2_OVERNIGHT_FLATTEN on a Webull leg do a fresh pair read (429 -> refused, pair untouched; filled child -> the #1046 durable path), cancel the pair, then the existing EH sell: LIMIT, session PM/AM, bid x (1 - oms_v2_exit_eh_protective_limit_buffer_pct/100) capped at the bid, never market, floor/stop kept as reference_price (APUS control 10.05 -> 10.00, ref 10.10); retry every 10 s while fillable and not dedup-active through 20:00; the confirmation exit stays refused after hours; Schwab untouched; GIPR double-cancel still fixed. T1: both after-hours tests now pin _is_regular_market_session and _extended_hours_session at module level; probed with the clock pinned to a 10:00 ET weekday, they stay green. T2: the confirmation-exit control pins _market_is_fillable=True and a None-returning fetch_oco_exit_fill; adding CONFIRMATION_EXIT to the EH-allowed set now fails it on cancel_pair_calls. S1: at >= 20:00 ET with the sell still latched and unsold, one critical SystemIncident (source webull_eh_ladder_unsold, deduped per managed_row_id, row-guarded) is written and the INC1 watch body/allowlist deliver it; disabling the page -> RED. Mutations at head, all reverted: EH guard removed -> RED; sell at the floor instead of bid-buffer -> RED; fresh pair read skipped -> 2 RED; confirmation exit allowed -> RED; page disabled -> RED. 278/278 across 7 test files; the single coroutine warning reproduces at base (pytest-asyncio teardown of a tracked task). Body states the 09:30 RTH-edge re-arm already reaches a prior-day bare share (flag true on the box) and the flatten floor-discard nit. Non-blocking: the EH retry latch is in-memory (an OMS restart between the last attempt and the first post-20:00 sweep loses the page); the release-site fillable half is dominated by an earlier gate (unexercised); the dedup scan loads all service incidents per sweep after 20:00. Not deployed.
